title: Rendering performance
text: Three use cases, range sizes: Large time series: one scattergl line trace date-time x (1 s steps) random walk y. 10 time series: ten scattergl line traces, one per column wide data frame, sharing date-time x. plotly.core sends array repeated figure (see widget_to_JSON()), x sent rather ten times. Large matrix heatmap: one heatmap trace n × n matrix. Metrics: Build + write (s): R Python time figure-making call standalone HTML page written disk (htmlwidgets::saveWidget() plot_ly(), write_html() go_figure(), fig.write_html() Python), one untimed warm-run, fresh process per variant. HTML (MB): size page, holds figure data (plotly.js separate file). Load time (s): headless Chrome, navigation start first frame painted plotly.js’s newPlot() resolves. Pages served HTTP localhost browser cache disabled, time covers fetching parsing plotly.js page, decoding data plotting, network latency. newPlot (s): time plotly.js spends newPlot(), part load time. Peak renderer memory (MB): largest resident memory page’s renderer process loading, sampled every 20 ms. JS heap load (MB): JavaScript heap use load forced garbage collection, plus array buffers (Chrome reports ).
code: library(plotly.core)  run <- isTRUE(as.logical(Sys.getenv("PLOTLY_CORE_RUN_BENCHMARKS", "false"))) wd <- normalizePath(params$workdir, mustWork = FALSE) results_dir <- params$results_dir # relative to this file, as pkgdown renders it from another directory doc_dir <- Sys.getenv("QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH") if (!dir.exists(results_dir) && nzchar(doc_dir)) {   results_dir <- file.path(doc_dir, results_dir) } pages_dir <- file.path(wd, "pages") reps <- params$reps variants <- c("release", "core_backend", "go_figure_f32", "plotly_py", "plotly_py_f32") dir.create(file.path(wd, "data"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) dir.create(pages_dir, showWarnings = FALSE) dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)  release_lib <- if (nzchar(params$release_lib)) params$release_lib else file.path(wd, "lib-release") core_lib <- if (nzchar(params$core_lib)) params$core_lib else .libPaths()[1] if (!file.exists(file.path(release_lib, "plotly", "DESCRIPTION"))) {   dir.create(release_lib, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)   install.packages("plotly", lib = release_lib, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org",                    type = "source", dependencies = FALSE) } libs <- list(release = release_lib, core_backend = core_lib, go_figure_f32 = core_lib) python <- params$python

title: Rendering performance
text: data generated R written little-endian doubles, every variant (R Python) plots values.
code: cases <- rbind(   data.frame(case = "timeseries", size = params$ts_sizes, values = params$ts_sizes),   data.frame(case = "multiseries", size = params$ms_sizes, values = params$ms_sizes * 10),   data.frame(case = "heatmap", size = params$hm_sizes, values = params$hm_sizes^2) ) cases$file <- file.path(wd, "data", sprintf("%s-%d.bin", cases$case, cases$size)) set.seed(2024) for (i in seq_len(nrow(cases))) {   n <- cases$size[i]   v <- if (cases$case[i] == "timeseries") {     cumsum(rnorm(n))   } else if (cases$case[i] == "multiseries") {     as.vector(apply(matrix(rnorm(n * 10), n), 2, cumsum))   } else {     s <- seq(0, 6 * pi, length.out = n)     as.vector(outer(sin(s), cos(s)) + rnorm(n * n, sd = 0.1))   }   writeBin(v, cases$file[i], endian = "little") }

title: Rendering performance
text: R code variant. Every function gets time series t (POSIXct, UTC) y; 10 series data frame d columns t y01, …, y10; heatmap matrix z. plotly.py equivalents (plotly_py_f32 converts arrays astype(np.float32) timing starts, as_float32() marks ):
code: figures <- list(   release = list(     timeseries = function(t, y) plot_ly(x = t, y = y, type = "scattergl", mode = "lines"),     multiseries = function(d) {       p <- plot_ly(d, x = ~t)       for (col in names(d)[-1]) {         p <- add_trace(p, y = d[[col]], name = col, type = "scattergl", mode = "lines")       }       p     },     heatmap = function(z) plot_ly(z = z, type = "heatmap")   ),   go_figure_f32 = list(     timeseries = function(t, y) {       go_figure() |> add_scattergl(x = t, y = as_float32(y), mode = "lines")     },     multiseries = function(d) {       fig <- go_figure()       for (col in names(d)[-1]) {         fig <- add_scattergl(fig, x = d$t, y = as_float32(d[[col]]), name = col, mode = "lines")       }       fig     },     heatmap = function(z) go_figure() |> add_heatmap(z = as_float32(z))   ) ) # the same plot_ly() code, run with the development plotly figures$core_backend <- figures$release  # how each variant writes its page writers <- list(   release = function(p, file) htmlwidgets::saveWidget(p, file, selfcontained = FALSE, libdir = "lib"),   core_backend = function(p, file) htmlwidgets::saveWidget(p, file, selfcontained = FALSE, libdir = "lib"),   go_figure_f32 = function(fig, file) write_html(fig, file, selfcontained = FALSE, libdir = "lib") ) import gc, json, sys, time import numpy as np, pandas as pd, plotly.graph_objects as go  variant, cases_file, reps, outdir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4] f32 = variant == "plotly_py_f32"  def timeseries(t, y):     return go.Figure(go.Scattergl(x=t, y=y, mode="lines"))  def multiseries(t, Y):     fig = go.Figure()     for j in range(Y.shape[1]):         fig.add_trace(go.Scattergl(x=t, y=Y[:, j], name=f"y{j + 1:02d}", mode="lines"))     return fig  def heatmap(z):     return go.Figure(go.Heatmap(z=z))  out = [] for case in json.load(open(cases_file)):     n, kind = case["size"], case["case"]     v = np.fromfile(case["file"], dtype="<f8")     if f32:         v = v.astype(np.float32)     if kind == "timeseries":         args = (pd.date_range("2024-01-01", periods=n, freq="s"), v)         make = timeseries     elif kind == "multiseries":         args = (pd.date_range("2024-01-01", periods=n, freq="s"), v.reshape((n, 10), order="F"))         make = multiseries     else:         args = (v.reshape((n, n), order="F"),)         make = heatmap     page = f"{outdir}/{kind}-{n}.html"     save = lambda: make(*args).write_html(page, include_plotlyjs="directory", full_html=True)     save()  # warm-up; also the page the browser loads     for rep in range(reps):         gc.collect()         t0 = time.perf_counter()         save()         out.append(dict(variant=variant, case=kind, size=n, rep=rep + 1,                         build_sec=time.perf_counter() - t0)) json.dump(out, sys.stdout)

title: Rendering performance
text: variant runs fresh process: R variants callr library holding right plotly version first library path.
code: r_worker <- function(variant, fns, write, cases, reps, outdir) {   suppressPackageStartupMessages(     if (variant == "go_figure_f32") library(plotly.core) else library(plotly)   )   dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)   out <- list()   for (i in seq_len(nrow(cases))) {     n <- cases$size[i]     v <- readBin(cases$file[i], "double", n = cases$values[i], endian = "little")     t <- as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC") + seq_len(n) - 1     if (cases$case[i] == "timeseries") {       args <- list(t = t, y = v)     } else if (cases$case[i] == "multiseries") {       y <- matrix(v, n, 10, dimnames = list(NULL, sprintf("y%02d", 1:10)))       args <- list(d = data.frame(t = t, y))     } else {       args <- list(z = matrix(v, n, n))     }     make <- fns[[cases$case[i]]]     page <- file.path(outdir, sprintf("%s-%d.html", cases$case[i], n))     save <- function() write(do.call(make, args), page)     save() # warm-up; also the page the browser loads     for (rep in seq_len(reps)) {       gc()       out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(         variant = variant, case = cases$case[i], size = n, rep = rep,         build_sec = system.time(save())[["elapsed"]]       )     }   }   do.call(rbind, out) }  build_r <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(figures), function(v) {   callr::r(r_worker, list(v, figures[[v]], writers[[v]], cases, reps, file.path(pages_dir, v)),            libpath = c(libs[[v]], .libPaths())) })) cases_json <- file.path(wd, "cases.json") jsonlite::write_json(cases[c("case", "size", "file")], cases_json) build_py <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("plotly_py", "plotly_py_f32"), function(v) {   outdir <- file.path(pages_dir, v)   dir.create(outdir, showWarnings = FALSE)   res <- system2(python, c(shQuote(file.path(wd, "bench.py")), v, shQuote(cases_json), reps,                            shQuote(outdir)), stdout = TRUE)   jsonlite::fromJSON(paste(res, collapse = "")) })) build <- rbind(build_r, build_py) pages <- expand.grid(variant = variants, i = seq_len(nrow(cases)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) pages <- cbind(pages["variant"], cases[pages$i, c("case", "size", "values")]) pages$path <- sprintf("%s/%s-%d.html", pages$variant, pages$case, pages$size) pages$html_mb <- file.size(file.path(pages_dir, pages$path)) / 1e6

title: Rendering performance
text: script injected page script runs wraps plotly.js’s newPlot()/react()/plot() time first plot, marks first frame painted : Results run 2026-11-14 macOS 26.5.1 (Apple M3 Pro), R version 4.4.2 (2024-10-31) Chrome/157.0.8103.78 (headless), versions:
code: (function () {   var B = window.__bench = { done: false };   function finish() {     if (B.end != null) return;     B.end = performance.now();     requestAnimationFrame(function () {       setTimeout(function () { B.painted = performance.now(); B.done = true; }, 0);     });   }   // plotly.js 3+ exports are read-only, so the wrapper is a new object   // inheriting from Plotly, with timed newPlot()/react()/plot()   function wrap(P) {     if (!P || P.__benchWrapped) return P;     var W = Object.create(P);     ["newPlot", "react", "plot"].forEach(function (k) {       var orig = P[k];       if (typeof orig !== "function") return;       W[k] = function () {         if (B.start == null) B.start = performance.now();         var r = orig.apply(P, arguments);         Promise.resolve(r).then(finish, function (e) { B.error = String(e); B.done = true; });         return r;       };     });     W.__benchWrapped = true;     return W;   }   var plotly;   Object.defineProperty(window, "Plotly", {     configurable: true,     get: function () { return plotly; },     set: function (v) { plotly = wrap(v); }   });   window.addEventListener("error", function (e) { B.error = String(e.message); B.done = true; }); })(); hook_js <- paste(readLines(file.path(wd, "hook.js")), collapse = "\n") chrome <- chromote::Chromote$new()  # serve the pages over HTTP from localhost port <- httpuv::randomPort() server <- callr::r_bg(function(dir, port) httpuv::runStaticServer(dir, port = port, browse = FALSE),                       list(pages_dir, port)) for (i in 1:50) {   if (!inherits(try(suppressWarnings(readLines(sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/", port), n = 1)),                     silent = TRUE), "try-error")) break   Sys.sleep(0.1) }  # samples the largest renderer process's memory (RSS) every 20 ms until killed sampler <- function(browser_pid, out) {   peak <- 0   repeat {     procs <- try(ps::ps_children(ps::ps_handle(browser_pid), recursive = TRUE), silent = TRUE)     if (!inherits(procs, "try-error")) {       for (p in procs) {         rss <- try({           if (any(grepl("--type=renderer", ps::ps_cmdline(p), fixed = TRUE))) ps::ps_memory_info(p)[["rss"]] else 0         }, silent = TRUE)         if (is.numeric(rss) && rss > peak) {           peak <- rss           writeLines(format(peak, scientific = FALSE), out)         }       }     }     Sys.sleep(0.02)   } } browser_pid <- chrome$get_browser()$get_process()$get_pid()  measure_page <- function(url, timeout = 300) {   s <- chromote::ChromoteSession$new(parent = chrome, width = 1000, height = 600)   on.exit(s$close(), add = TRUE)   s$Network$enable()   s$Network$setCacheDisabled(cacheDisabled = TRUE)   s$Page$enable() # needed for the injected script to run   s$Page$addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument(source = hook_js)   peak_file <- tempfile()   smp <- callr::r_bg(sampler, list(browser_pid, peak_file))   on.exit(smp$kill(), add = TRUE)   Sys.sleep(0.3) # let the sampler start   s$Page$navigate(url, wait_ = FALSE) # large pages can take a while to commit   t0 <- Sys.time()   repeat {     done <- s$Runtime$evaluate("!!(window.__bench && window.__bench.done)", timeout_ = timeout)$result$value     if (isTRUE(done)) break     if (difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs") > timeout) stop("timed out loading ", url)     Sys.sleep(0.05)   }   Sys.sleep(0.3)   smp$kill()   b <- jsonlite::fromJSON(s$Runtime$evaluate(     "JSON.stringify(Object.assign({}, window.__bench, {js_bytes: performance.getEntriesByType('resource')        .filter(e => /\\.js$/.test(e.name)).reduce((a, e) => a + e.encodedBodySize, 0)}))"   )$result$value)   if (!is.null(b$error)) stop(url, ": ", b$error)   s$HeapProfiler$collectGarbage()   heap <- s$Runtime$getHeapUsage()   data.frame(     load_sec = b$painted / 1000,     newplot_sec = (b$end - b$start) / 1000,     js_mb = b$js_bytes / 1e6,     peak_renderer_mb = as.numeric(readLines(peak_file, warn = FALSE)) / 1e6,     js_heap_mb = (heap$usedSize + if (is.null(heap$backingStorageSize)) 0 else heap$backingStorageSize) / 1e6   ) }  # on a failure (e.g. Chrome not responding), restart Chrome and try the page once more measure_retry <- function(url) {   tryCatch(measure_page(url), error = function(e) {     message("retrying ", url, " after: ", conditionMessage(e))     try(chrome$close(), silent = TRUE)     chrome <<- chromote::Chromote$new()     browser_pid <<- chrome$get_browser()$get_process()$get_pid()     measure_page(url)   }) }  set.seed(1) browser <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(reps), function(rep) {   # shuffle the page order each round, so drift doesn't favour a variant   do.call(rbind, lapply(sample(nrow(pages)), function(i) {     cbind(pages[i, c("variant", "case", "size")], rep = rep,           measure_retry(sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/%s", port, pages$path[i])))   })) })) server$kill() r_versions <- function(lib) {   callr::r(function() {     js_version <- function(pkg, file) {       f <- system.file("htmlwidgets", "lib", "plotlyjs", file, package = pkg)       if (!nzchar(f)) return(NA_character_)       head <- readChar(f, 500)       sub("^v", "", regmatches(head, regexpr("v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+", head)))     }     # the development plotly draws with plotly.core's plotly.js     uses_core <- grepl("plotly.core", utils::packageDescription("plotly")$Imports, fixed = TRUE)     data.frame(       plotly = as.character(utils::packageVersion("plotly")),       plotly.core = if (uses_core) as.character(utils::packageVersion("plotly.core")) else NA,       plotly.js = if (uses_core) js_version("plotly.core", "plotly.min.js") else js_version("plotly", "plotly-latest.min.js")     )   }, libpath = c(lib, .libPaths())) } py <- jsonlite::fromJSON(system2(python, c("-c", shQuote(paste(   "import json, plotly, numpy, pandas, plotly.offline as o;",   "print(json.dumps(dict(plotly=plotly.__version__, numpy=numpy.__version__,",   "pandas=pandas.__version__, plotlyjs=o.get_plotlyjs_version())))"))), stdout = TRUE)) versions <- rbind(   cbind(variant = "release", r_versions(release_lib)),   cbind(variant = "core_backend, go_figure_f32", r_versions(core_lib)),   data.frame(variant = "plotly_py, plotly_py_f32",              plotly = paste0(py$plotly, " (Python; numpy ", py$numpy, ", pandas ", py$pandas, ")"),              plotly.core = NA, plotly.js = py$plotlyjs) ) cpu <- if (Sys.info()[["sysname"]] == "Darwin") {   system("sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string", intern = TRUE) } else {   NA_character_ } meta <- list(date = format(Sys.Date()), R = R.version.string, os = utils::sessionInfo()$running,              cpu = cpu, browser = chrome$Browser$getVersion()$product, reps = reps) chrome$close()  write.csv(build, file.path(results_dir, "build.csv"), row.names = FALSE) write.csv(browser, file.path(results_dir, "browser.csv"), row.names = FALSE) write.csv(pages[c("variant", "case", "size", "values", "html_mb")], file.path(results_dir, "pages.csv"), row.names = FALSE) write.csv(versions, file.path(results_dir, "versions.csv"), row.names = FALSE) jsonlite::write_json(meta, file.path(results_dir, "meta.json"), auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)

code: med <- function(d, cols) aggregate(d[cols], d[c("variant", "case", "size")], median) res <- merge(merge(med(build, "build_sec"), pages),              med(browser, c("load_sec", "newplot_sec", "js_mb", "peak_renderer_mb", "js_heap_mb"))) res$variant <- factor(res$variant, variants) res$case <- factor(res$case, c("timeseries", "multiseries", "heatmap")) res <- res[order(res$case, res$size, res$variant), ] res$label <- ifelse(res$case == "heatmap", paste0(res$size, "²"), format(res$size, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)) res$label[res$case == "multiseries"] <- paste("10 ×", res$label[res$case == "multiseries"])  show_table <- function(case) {   d <- res[res$case == case, ]   knitr::kable(     d[c("label", "variant", "build_sec", "html_mb", "load_sec", "newplot_sec", "js_mb", "peak_renderer_mb", "js_heap_mb")],     col.names = c("size", "variant", "build + write (s)", "HTML (MB)", "load (s)", "newPlot (s)",                   "JS transferred (MB)", "peak renderer (MB)", "JS heap after (MB)"),     digits = c(0, 0, 3, 2, 3, 3, 2, 0, 1), row.names = FALSE   ) } show_table("timeseries") show_table("multiseries") show_table("heatmap") chart_metrics <- c(`build + write (s)` = "build_sec", `HTML (MB)` = "html_mb", `load (s)` = "load_sec",                    `newPlot (s)` = "newplot_sec", `peak renderer (MB)` = "peak_renderer_mb",                    `JS heap after (MB)` = "js_heap_mb") long <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(col, name) {   data.frame(res[c("variant", "case", "values")], metric = name, value = res[[col]]) }, chart_metrics, names(chart_metrics))) long <- long[order(long$variant, long$case, long$values), ]  fig <- px_line(   long, x = "values", y = "value", color = "variant",   facet_row = "metric", facet_col = "case", markers = TRUE, log_x = TRUE, log_y = TRUE,   category_orders = list(variant = variants, metric = names(chart_metrics), case = levels(res$case)),   # R in blues, Python in oranges; the darkest of each is the float32 variant   color_discrete_map = list(release = "#6baed6", core_backend = "#2171b5", go_figure_f32 = "#08306b",                             plotly_py = "#fd8d3c", plotly_py_f32 = "#a63603"),   labels = list(values = "values plotted", value = "", variant = ""),   facet_row_spacing = 0.03, template = "plotly_white", height = 1400 ) # each panel gets its own axis range: the metrics differ by orders of magnitude for (ax in grep("^[xy]axis", names(fig$layout), value = TRUE)) {   fig$layout[[ax]]$matches <- NULL   fig$layout[[ax]]$showticklabels <- TRUE   if (startsWith(ax, "x")) fig$layout[[ax]]$dtick <- 1 # a tick per power of 10 } fig |>   for_each_annotation(function(a) {     a$text <- sub("^[^=]*=", "", a$text) # "case=heatmap" -> "heatmap"     a   }) |>   update_layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = 1.03, yanchor = "bottom", x = 0)) |>   partial_bundle("auto") metrics <- c(`build + write` = "build_sec", HTML = "html_mb", load = "load_sec",              `peak renderer` = "peak_renderer_mb", `JS heap` = "js_heap_mb") base <- res[res$variant == "release", c("case", "size", metrics)] rel <- merge(res[res$variant != "release", c("variant", "case", "size", "label", metrics)], base,              by = c("case", "size"), suffixes = c("", ".release")) for (m in metrics) rel[[m]] <- rel[[paste0(m, ".release")]] / rel[[m]] rel <- rel[order(rel$case, rel$size, rel$variant), ] knitr::kable(rel[c("case", "label", "variant", metrics)],              col.names = c("case", "size", "variant", names(metrics)), digits = 1, row.names = FALSE)

what: Create Interactive Web Graphics via plotly.js
title: Create Interactive Web Graphics via plotly.js
text: Interactive web graphics R built plotly.js. plotly.core rendering engine plotly R package can also used stand-alone. Faster plots, less browser memory plotly.core leverages advances plotly.js improve browser rendering performance, implements optimizations R backend cut plot generation time size memory. Rendering large time series plots heatmaps 10-100x faster. DateTime optimizations support single precision floats allows 2x reduction browser memory. (See render-performance vignette details) Machine-generated code documentation plotly.js schema. 47 trace types every layout object machine-generated go_*() constructor (go_scatter(),go_layout_xaxis(), … 979 total) comprehensive R documentation arguments thorough validation generated schema. Future changes plotly.js schema can ported R implementation without hand-writing R code documentation. Full backwards compatibility plotly R package. plotly’s plot_ly() ggplotly() plots rendered plotly.core, existing plotly R code gets performance work plotly.js version. (Working branch: msummersgill/plotly@plotly-core-render) Helper functions plotly package back-port functionality features behavior deprecated last CRAN release plotly.js/2.25.2 plotly-js/latest Shiny, R Markdown, Quarto, static image export plotlyOutput()/renderPlotly(), event_data() plotlyProxy() work plotly R package; figures render inline documents, static images PDF/Word output.save_image() exports PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG PDF Kaleido. Plotly Express Ports functionality plotly.py package introduce high-level methods quickly create figures minimal code.

title: Send numeric data to the browser in single precision — as_float32
text: Single precision keeps 7 significant digits: values shown hover labels returned event_data() change (0.1 becomes 0.100000001490116), whole numbers 2^24 (16,777,216) exact numeric times seconds since 1970 accurate minutes. title: Funnel traces — add_funnel
text: Visualize stages process using length-encoded bars. trace can used show data either part--whole representation wherein item appears single stage, "drop-" representation wherein item appears stage traversed. See also "funnelarea" trace type different approach visualizing funnel data.

title: Splom traces — add_splom
text: Splom traces generate scatter plot matrix visualizations. splom `dimensions` items correspond generated axis. Values dimensions set `dimensions[].values`. Splom traces support `scattergl` marker style attributes. Specify `layout.grid` attributes /layout x-axis y-axis attributes control axis positioning style.
